alignments.note: Waw of the consecutive form takes the ASV's connective under rule 14.
Construct noun with no article morpheme present, so the ASV's *the* is supplied onto it under rule 29.
Nomen rectum carries the relational *of* under rule 19, headed on the name.

`צָלַח` is rendered *came mightily*; headed on the lexical predicate *came* under rule 24. The competing reading heads on *mightily* under rule 44's light-verb test, since *came* alone is any coming; taken as a full lexical verb rather than a light verb.
Preposition takes its own English word.
Pronominal suffix takes the object pronoun under rule 18.
Waw takes the written *and* under rule 14.
Finite verb with its subject pronoun under rule 17, headed on the lexical verb.
Object suffix takes the object pronoun under rule 18.
Comparative preposition takes the written *as*.
Infinitive construct after `כְּ`; the supplied subject pronoun and modal belong to the infinitive under rules 48 and 52, while the preposition keeps only *as*.
Article morpheme with no *the* written for the phrase — the ASV renders *a kid* — so `unrepresented` under rule 29.
The indefinite article belongs to the noun that licenses it under rule 15.
Waw takes the written *and*.

Supplied possessive recasting of an existential clause. Rule 43's count finds no morpheme to carry the *have*: no `הָיָה`, no possessive preposition (the `בְּ` is spent on *in*), no unspent suffix (the suffix is spent on *his*), and no verb the *have* renders — the same shape as `אוֹ תְבַלֻּל בְּעֵינוֹ` → *or that hath a blemish in his eye*. The supplied subject *he* stands with it as one unit under rule 2. The competing reading gives *had* to the existential `אַיִן` as rule 50's frame, but that rule places a supplied dummy, not a referential subject.

One English word for the indefinite `מְאוּמָה` and the existential negative, exactly the `לֹא־יִדְבַּק בְּיָדְךָ מְאוּמָה` → *nought* case of rule 35; headed on the negative, which is what distinguishes *nothing* from *aught*.
Preposition takes its own word.
Suffix takes the possessive pronoun under rule 18.
Noun takes its own word.
Waw rendered by the adversative *but*, which rule 14's open list covers.
Negative takes the written *not*; the unit is discontinuous from the verb under rule 25.
Finite verb with its subject pronoun under rule 17.
Dative `לְ` rendered as a bare English indirect object — *told not his father* — so `unrepresented` under rule 40.
Suffix takes the possessive under rule 18.
Noun takes its own word.
Waw rendered by *or* under rule 14's open list of connectives.
Second dative `לְ` likewise left with no English word under rule 40.
Suffix takes the possessive under rule 18.
Noun takes its own word.
Object marker with no English word spent on the object relation, which is rule 16's ordinary ruling.
Headless relative rendered by *what*; the relative morpheme is written, so rule 46's first rider gives it the word.
Finite verb with its subject pronoun and auxiliary under rule 17, headed on the lexical verb.

review_notes: The supplied *he had* of the third colon is the verse's one contested unit: rule 43's count leaves it unlicensed because the `בְּ` and its suffix are both already spent on *in his hand*, while rule 50 would offer it to the existential `אַיִן`. Recorded as `added` with the competing reading named in the unit's note.
`מְאוּמָה` and `אֵין` are fused on the single *nothing* under rule 35 rather than split with one member `unrepresented`.
